Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-03-04):
- History: Prices declining from 82.94 → 71.55 over ~18 days
- Model forecasts vs true outcomes divergence:
  - Days 1-5: Model close to true (differences < 0.5)
  - Days 6-10: Model starts underestimating more noticeably
  - Days 11-15: Model is consistently ~3-5 points lower than true
  - Days 16-20: Model ~4.5-5 points lower
  - Days 21-25: Model ~4-5.3 points lower
  - Days 26-30: Model ~5.3-6.25 points lower

Looking at Example 2 (2025-03-03):
- Very similar pattern - model is ~3-6 points lower than true in the latter half

Looking at Example 3 (2025-02-28):
- Same pattern - model underestimates by 3-6 points in days 11-30

Looking at Example 4 (2025-01-22):
- Prices are higher (~78-88 range)
- Model forecasts vs true outcomes:
  - Days 1-5: Very close (differences < 0.1)
  - Days 6-10: Model starts being slightly lower but not by much
  - Days 11-15: Model ~0.3-0.7 points lower
  - Days 16-20: Model ~1.3-2.0 points lower
  - Days 21-25: Model ~2.0-2.9 points lower
  - Days 26-30: Model ~3.6-6.9 points lower

Looking at Example 5 (2025-01-21):
- Almost identical to Example 4


- Model underestimates by 3-6 points in days 11-30

I've identified a consistent pattern of model underperformance across multiple examples. The divergence appears to intensify as we move further into the forecast horizon, with differences escalating from minimal at the start to more significant deviations of 3-6 points in the latter days. This suggests a systematic bias in the model's forecasting ability, particularly as predictions extend beyond 10 days.
